name: Andy Barr

issue_poll.name: Change Research for Kentucky Center for Economic Policy, Kentucky registered voters (n=2,079), Dec 1-5, 2025 - most important issues (pick up to three)
issue_poll.note: No full issue ranking from a fall 2026 Kentucky poll was found. Used the most complete state ranking (Dec 2025). Rank 10 was a tie between K-12 education and democracy/voting rights (10% each); broken toward democracy because Emerson's Feb 2026 Kentucky poll put threats to democracy 3rd (13.5%) behind economy (38.8%) and health care (14.5%) (https://www.lex18.com/news/state-of-the-commonwealth/kentucky-senate-race-wide-open-as-new-poll-shows-most-voters-still-undecided). Poll was sponsored by a left-leaning policy group; the issue list is standard.

issues.detail: Lower energy costs by restarting closed coal plants, faster energy permitting, blocking plant closures without grid-reliability review
No Social Security changes affecting current retirees; bipartisan reforms for future retirees, unspecified
Cut taxes; no specific measures or amounts
Market-based reform increasing insurer competition and choice; oppose government-run health care
Deport people in the country illegally; prioritize border security; streamline legal immigration programs
Protect Second Amendment rights; oppose gun control; no specific measure
Increase housing supply; loosen rules on community banks and mortgage lenders; back pending housing supply bill
Support DOGE federal spending cuts; cut spending on programs deemed unneeded
Support police funding; oppose anti-police policies; no specific measure
Pass SAVE America Act: photo voter ID and documentary proof of citizenship to vote in federal elections

plan_caveats: Could not confirm the Nov 3, 2026 general-election result from a source; winner status taken from the task.
Issue poll is from Dec 2025, not close to Election Day; no fall 2026 Kentucky issue ranking found.
Campaign site has only three issue pages (coal plan, military and veterans, law enforcement); the issues index page could not be fetched.
Elections rating relies on a Feb 2026 official House-office release urging Senate passage, plus Barr's campaign-season X post, not a campaign-site page.
Energy plan items (grid-reliability review, energy financing access) could read as Concrete energy policy, but their link to cost of living is direction only, so rated Partial.
Social Security pledge (no changes for current retirees) comes from a June 2026 local news report of a campaign stop; Medicare not addressed.
Barr's many House votes and bills (Stop Chinese Fentanyl Act, Secure the Border Act, Fair Access to Banking Act) were excluded as past record.
Barr skipped the April 2026 KET primary debate; the Oct 2026 WKYT general debate coverage reported no specific commitments on most top issues.
